subject: Eval success criteria & trial runbook — Skyline Analytics POC
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@skyline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval success criteria & trial runbook — Skyline Analytics POC

Tom — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed success criteria + next steps so we can lock the POC runway.

Call summary (TL;DR)
- Goal: validate Redwood integration for Skyline's document-enrichment pipelines (classification + extractive summarization) at production throughput and latency while keeping token economics within target.
- Scope: representative dataset (approx 3k requests) provided by Skyline; two-phase run (smoke -> full eval).

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Quality (primary)
   - Human-eval pass rate >= 88% on Skyline verification set (binary accept/reject on key extraction + relevance).
   - Automated QA: precision >= 0.85, recall >= 0.80 on labeled subset.
2) Latency (SLO)
   - P95 end-to-end inference latency < 300 ms for requests <= 512 tokens (measured after warm-up, steady-state).
3) Throughput (capacity)
   - Sustained throughput: 30 requests/sec.
   - Burst capability: handle short bursts up to 120 requests/sec with graceful degradation (queue/backpressure).
4) Cost (economics)
   - Target average cost <= $0.0025 per token (target for unit economics modeling; final billing cadence TBD).

Evaluation plan
- Smoke: 3 business days (connect, validate connectivity, smoke tests).
- Baseline: 2 weeks (run canonical workloads, collect telemetry).
- Full evaluation: 4 weeks (run expanded sample set, human eval, regression checks).
- Accept when quality + SLOs met for 3 consecutive days in evaluation window.

Ownership (Redwood / Skyline)
- Redwood technical lead: Ben Carter — infra + runbook / performance tuning.
- Redwood solutions eng: Rishi Malhotra — pipelines, prompt engineering, evaluation harness.
- Redwood CSM: Monica Patel — timeline coordination, success criteria sign-off.
- Skyline: Tom Ellis (POC owner), Priya Shah (security lead), procurement@skyline.ai (contracts).

Next steps (action items):
- Redwood: share Mutual Action Plan and KPI template (attached).
- Skyline: send representative sample workload + expected QPS distribution (attach skyline_expected_workload.yaml).
- Schedule kickoff: propose week of Jun 14 for smoke run.
- Security: we will route your security contact Priya to our compliance team for SOC2 questionnaire.

Attachments: skyline_mutual_action_plan.xlsx, initial_kpi_template.csv

Thanks — I’ll wait for the sample workload and confirmation on the proposed timeline.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aisha.rahman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@skyline.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Jun 2027 16:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Eval success criteria & trial runbook — Skyline Analytics POC

Aisha — thanks for the thorough recap. This aligns well with what we discussed. A couple clarifications before we sign off:

1) Latency measurement window: when you say P95 < 300 ms, is that the P95 measured over 1-minute rolling windows, or overall across the evaluation period? We prefer the 1-minute rolling window to avoid noisy spikes.

2) Cost assumptions: our average request tends to be ~650 tokens (input+output). Can you confirm the $0.0025/token assumption and whether that includes tokenization inefficiencies? Also, do you assume streaming vs batch for those numbers?

3) Throughput expectations: the 30 RPS sustained target is fine; we will provide our hourly distribution. We also want to understand how Redwood handles cold KV-cache effects and whether you can guarantee warm-up periods for the smoke run.

Looping in our security lead Priya Shah (priya.shah@skyline.ai) and procurement (procurement@skyline.ai) so they can triage the compliance and contracting items. I attached our expected_workload.yaml — contains request size distribution and QPS curves.

If we can align on (1) rolling-window P95, (2) cost per token definition, and (3) a clear warm-up plan, we can greenlight the Jun 14 kickoff.

—Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of ML Infrastructure | Skyline Analytics
tom.ellis@skyline.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@skyline.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval success criteria & trial runbook — Skyline Analytics POC

Thanks Tom — good questions. Internal note and proposed playbook below (cc'd Tom to keep us aligned).

1) Measurement framing
   - We will measure P95 on 1-minute rolling windows during steady-state (explicitly excluding an initial 10-minute warm-up window at the start of any smoke or evaluation run). That addresses the cold-KV/cache concern.

2) Cost assumptions
   - $0.0025/token is our target list estimate for the model configuration we discussed (quantized 16-bit weights + aggressive KV caching). That number assumes streaming token output and typical tokenization overhead; for 650-token average requests this maps to ~$1.62/request. We'll run a small billing-sim during baseline to confirm.

3) Throughput and resilience
   - Sustained: 30 RPS.
   - Burst: 120 RPS for up to 90 seconds with queueing/backoff.

4) Ops and mitigations (how we meet SLOs)
   - Warm-up: run a 10-minute warm-up with synthetic requests that mirror the payload distribution (we'll provide a warm-up generator in ops_runbook.md).
   - Caching: prefix + KV caching for repeated contexts; improves cost and latency for multi-step sessions.
   - Autoscale policy: can scale compute within 60–90 seconds depending on call pattern; we’ll instrument burst telemetry to avoid overprovisioning.

Ownership & milestones (dates are tentative):
- Jun 9: Redwood sends final Mutual Action Plan and Ops runbook (Ben).
- Jun 11: Skyline shares expected_workload.yaml + final list of evaluation queries (Tom).
- Jun 14: Kickoff smoke run (connectivity + warm-up).
- Jun 16–30: Baseline & tuning (Rishi + Skyline engs).
- Jul 1–28: Full evaluation + human eval.

Action items (who does what)
- Ben: finalize ops_runbook.md and warm-up tool (deliver Jun 9).
- Rishi: build evaluation harness and human-eval instructions (deliver Jun 11).
- Monica: coordinate weekly checkpoint calls and collect sign-offs (ongoing).
- Aisha: own commercial terms and procurement loop.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Aisha / team — we’re good to proceed on the items below. Confirming acceptance of the operational definitions:
- P95 measured on 1-minute rolling windows after a 10-minute warm-up.
- Target P95 ceiling: 300 ms for <=512-token requests.
- Sustained throughput 30 RPS; burst to 120 RPS with queueing/backoff.
- Cost target: $0.0025/token (we'll validate during baseline).

Priya will take point on security questions; please send the SOC2 questionnaire link to her (priya.shah@skyline.ai). Procurement will start the SOW review — I’ll push the DocuSign link once they have a first pass.

We’ll kick off smoke on Jun 14 as proposed. Looking forward to the runbook and KPI template.

Thanks — Tom
